newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Trostberg off to good start in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Trostberg off to good start in 1997.

text.p: SKW Trostberg AG, the world's largest construction chemicals firm, said Wednesday sales were climbing so far this year but warned a major acquistion in 1996 could hurt net profit.

SKW said in a statement that sales climbed 37 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 1.32 billion marks, but that without the purchase last autumn of Master Builders Technologies turnover would have climbed only four percent.
For the year as a whole, the company said it expected sales of over five billion marks, up from 3.9 billion marks, largely on the back of the MBT acquisition.
SKW bought MBT from Swiss chemicals group Sandoz AG SANZ.S late last year, paying 1.3 billion Swiss francs, 1.1 billion of which SKW paid in cash.
The company had said in the past that it would write off about half the cost of MBT over the next 15 years.
SKW, warned, that the cost of that acquisition could hurt net profit this year, trimming up to 50 million marks from 1996's 150 million mark net profit result.
But the company said it did not see a danger of a lower dividend than 1996's 22 percent and that it was aiming for pre-tax profit around the same as last year's 240 million marks.
The MBT acquisition should help profits in the years ahead, SKW said, adding it expected to report a operating return on sales of 10 percent, up from seven percent last year.
SKW said it would consider raising capital from the second half of this year but said that any such move was "not urgent".
The company reported in March that group profit from operating activities had climbed slightly to 286 million marks from 281 million marks.
Master Builders Technologies, however, did not have any impact on last year's result as MBT was not consolidated in SKW's accounts until December 31, 1996.
The company's earnings per share for the year according the DVFA accounting rules rose to 2.25 marks versus 2.03 marks in the previous year.
The firm also said its first quarter profits for 1997 were well above those made in the same period a year earlier.
